title: Eviction Orchestrator: Per-tenant Graceful Drain & Failover Policy for Private Clusters
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Why: Private and Dedicated customers expect predictable SLAs during control-plane maintenance, kernel upgrades, and region failovers. Today our rolling upgrades can induce noisy neighbor effects where a small subset of tenants triggers global CPU/queue pressure and causes disproportionate latency spikes for co-tenants. There is no unified mechanism to drain traffic from an affected tenant while preserving region-level SLOs or to coordinate fast failover without data-plane thrash.

Goal: Build an "Eviction Orchestrator" service and associated policies that enable: (1) per-tenant graceful drain (in-band and via control-plane signals), (2) an adaptive circuit-breaker and load-shedding policy that prefers tenant-scoped degradation over region-wide SLO violations, and (3) safe upgrade windows with automated canary fencing and operator runbooks for private/dedicated control planes. The feature must work for single-region private clusters and multi-region Dedicated setups.

High-level design:
- Tenant Scoring: continuous tenant health score computed from token error-rate, 99p latency, active concurrency, and KV cache hit rate. Scores are time-decayed and used to prioritize evictions.
- Evictor API: control-plane endpoint to mark a tenant for graceful drain with modes: SCHEDULED_DRAIN, EMERG_ISOLATE, REGION_FALLBACK. Draining signals propagate to dataplane routing layer via lease tokens.
- Lease Tokens & Heartbeats: short-lived tenant leases held by local dataplane nodes; a centralized coordinator can revoke leases to speed eviction and force routing to fallback region/variant.
- Circuit Breakers: tenant-scoped circuit breakers that trip based on composite SLO breach (error-rate OR p99 latency OR queue depth). When tripped, apply soft degradation: reduce concurrent routing tokens, route to cheaper model variants, enable compact quantized path, or shed low-priority requests.
- Load Shedding Policies: tiered policy engine that prefers: 1) shed background/low-priority work, 2) reduce batch concurrency for offender, 3) evict offender to isolated lane, 4) region-level shedding as last resort.
- Upgrade Safety: before control-plane upgrades, create a planned drain window that sequenced evictions by tenant-score and by region-affinity. Provide automatic canary fencing—during canary rollout, only allow a fixed traffic quota and prevent global cache invalidations.
- Observability & Runbooks: new dashboards (per-tenant SLO rollup, active evictions, tripped breakers), alerts for asymmetric eviction rates, and an operator runbook for manual override and rollback.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict tenant isolation increases complexity for autoscaling; we prefer lease-based soft-eviction to avoid abrupt re-scheduling cascades.
- Evicting a high-value tenant reduces short-term revenue impact; policy will include cost-aware weights so business-critical tenants are treated with guardrails.
- Stronger consistency of lease revocation requires lower heartbeat intervals which increases control-plane load; we'll use adaptive intervals based on cluster telemetry.

Success metrics:
- Reduce multi-tenant SLO breach window during upgrades by 80% in canary runs.
- Hit target: at least two-thirds of evictions complete gracefully (no 5xx spike) within configured drain window.
- Reduce region-level failover incidents caused by noisy neighbors by 90% on staging.

Implementation phases:
1) RFC and simulation harness (1 sprint): define scoring, tokens, and policy DSL.
2) Evictor API + lease token prototype behind feature flag (2 sprints).
3) Circuit-breaker and load-shed adapters in routing layer + canary tests (2 sprints).
4) Runbook, dashboards, and private cluster pilot (1 sprint).

Open questions:
- How do we encode business-priority weights and expose opt-outs to enterprise customers?
- What are safe defaults for drain windows per hardware profile?
- Should we provide a customer-visible API for self-eviction (customers preemptively draining their tenants)?

Rollout plan: internal-only flag → private cluster beta customers → opt-in dedicated regions → GA.

Notes: this ticket focuses on orchestration and policies. Dataplane adapters (routing token enforcement, model-variant fallbacks) will be separate implementation tickets linked as dependencies.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: flagged as P0 after incident post-upgrade in staging where three tenants saturated KV cache and triggered region-level failover. Assigned to Marcus for design leadership.

2026-03-03 - Design review: team agreed on lease-token approach over hard fencing to avoid cache thrash. Liam raised concern about heartbeat load; proposal to make heartbeat interval adaptive accepted.
2026-03-05 - PM sync: product asked for a business-priority field exposed in admin UI; decided to implement as opt-in metadata with default 0 (neutral). Will surface in RBAC-protected admin only.
2026-03-08 - Security: requested threat model for token revocation and lease spoofing. Security review required before pilot. Added to dependencies.
2026-03-10 - Prototype milestone: basic Evictor API implemented behind feature flag; simulated tenant-score in harness. Observability stubbed into existing SLO dashboards.
2026-03-12 - Next: create PRs for routing adapter and canary gating, draft operator runbook, schedule pilot with two private customers in 2026-04.
Blockers: security review for token lifecycle, and a small capacity increase in control-plane to support adaptive heartbeat under high tenant-count clusters.
